svg.title: From Beer Hall Putsch (Nov 1923) to Nationwide NSDAP Reorganisation (1924–28)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map of Weimar Germany (1923–28) with a street-scale Munich inset charting Hitler’s failed 8–9 November 1923 Beer Hall Putsch march from the Bürgerbräukeller to Odeonsplatz, Landsberg Fortress imprisonment, the February 1926 Bamberg Conference, July 1926 Weimar Rally, Goebbels’ appointment in Berlin, and the nationwide 35-Gau party network.

g.text: 1. MUNICH STREET PLAN • 8–9 NOV 1923 PUTSCH MARCH
Nov 1923 Putsch • 1924 trial & Mein Kampf • Feb 1925 relaunch
Regional Gauleiters bound by Bamberg Führerprinzip (1926)
Debt-hit farmers targeted after 2.6% (12-seat) urban vote
Odeonsplatz firefight: 16 Nazis & 4 Bavarian police killed

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · PAPER 3 (OPTION 31) · KT2.2: MUNICH PUTSCH & LEAN YEARS
From Beer Hall Putsch (Nov 1923) to Nationwide NSDAP Reorganisation (1924–28)
After the failed 8–9 Nov 1923 Munich Putsch (16 Nazis killed) & Landsberg prison (Mein Kampf), Hitler switched to legal elections (Feb 1925),
enforced the Führerprinzip at Bamberg (Feb 1926), and built a 35-Gau national machine ready to exploit crisis despite winning just 2.6% in May 1928.
